title: Deterministic near-linear-query approximation schemes for matroid intersection
formal: Is there a deterministic algorithm and absolute constants \(C,a,b>0\) that, given independence-oracle access to any two matroids on a common \(n\)-element ground set and any rational \(0<\varepsilon<1\), finds a common independent set of size at least \((1-\varepsilon)r\) using at most \(Cn\log^a(n+2)\varepsilon^{-b}\) oracle queries, where \(r\) is the maximum size of a common independent set?

why: The question asks whether random sampling is essential for information-efficient approximate intersection of arbitrary matroids. A positive answer would derandomize a central combinatorial optimization primitive at near-linear query cost; a negative answer would establish a separation in the power of adaptive deterministic and randomized oracle access.
status_note: Terao’s 2025 source explicitly leaves the deterministic near-linear independence-query approximation scheme open across general ranks. The checked 2026 result is for explicit linear matroid representations. No matching resolution for arbitrary independence oracles was located in the bounded September 2026 check.

importance.reason: A broad derandomization and oracle-efficiency question for a central combinatorial optimization primitive, covering all common ranks and arbitrary matroids.

sentences: Two unknown matroids are accessed only by tests of whether a proposed subset is independent.
The algorithm must output a large set independent in both matroids.
The target is deterministic approximation arbitrarily close to optimum with near-linear query complexity.
The guarantee must cover every common rank, without stronger rank queries or matrix representations.
Randomized near-linear schemes and a deterministic two-thirds approximation are known.

definitions: A matroid on \(V=[n]\) is a family \(\mathcal I\subseteq2^V\) containing the empty set, closed under taking subsets, and satisfying augmentation: if \(X,Y\in\mathcal I\) and \(|X|<|Y|\), some \(e\in Y\setminus X\) has \(X\cup\{e\}\in\mathcal I\). The two unknown families \(\mathcal I_1,\mathcal I_2\) are supplied through separate exact independence oracles. A query specifies an index \(j\in\{1,2\}\) and a subset \(S\subseteq[n]\), and returns one bit indicating whether \(S\in\mathcal I_j\). The total number of calls to both oracles is charged, including repeated calls. Queries may depend on all previous answers. The algorithm knows \(n\) and \(\varepsilon\), but need not be told \(r=\max\{|S|:S\in\mathcal I_1\cap\mathcal I_2\}\), and receives no representation, rank oracle or additional promise. It must output the elements of a feasible common independent set, not merely estimate \(r\). The guarantee must hold for every pair of matroids and every attainable \(0\leq r\leq n\); loops, parallel elements, unequal matroid ranks and rank zero are allowed. Computation between queries is unrestricted but finite, and the algorithm is deterministic and uniform over \(n\) and the binary accuracy parameter. The target measures query complexity rather than arithmetic or bit running time. The constants and exponents in the displayed bound are independent of the matroids, \(n,r\) and \(\varepsilon\).
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm with the stated feasibility, approximation and query bounds, or prove that no such deterministic approximation scheme exists in this oracle model. A randomized scheme, a nearly linear scheme only when the common rank is a constant fraction of n, or a scheme that uses stronger rank queries does not decide the target.

context_blocks.text: Terao’s 2025 paper explicitly asks whether deterministic near-linear-query approximation can approach one throughout the rank range. Its soft-O convention permits polynomial factors in inverse accuracy and logarithms of n; the displayed bound makes those factors explicit.

For two partition matroids representing the endpoints of a bipartite graph, common independent sets are matchings. General matroids can hide much more information behind each membership bit, so algorithms for explicitly represented graphs alone do not answer the oracle question.

A greedy maximal common independent set gives a one-half approximation with a linear number of independence queries. Terao improves the ratio to two thirds minus an accuracy term with O(n/ε+r log r) queries. This is a fixed approximation threshold, not an arbitrarily accurate scheme.

Blikstad and Tu achieve a near-linear-query randomized approximation scheme. Their work also provides a deterministic strictly linear-query guarantee in the large-common-rank regime for fixed accuracy. These results show why neither randomization nor the quantifier over all ranks can be omitted.

Terao’s 2026 algorithm for linear matroid intersection accesses two explicit matrices and exploits linear-algebraic structure. Its input-sparsity running time is a different resource guarantee and does not yield a deterministic near-linear membership-query algorithm for arbitrary matroids.

Taking ε very small eventually forces an exact answer because the output size is integral. This causes no contradiction with exact-intersection lower bounds: the allowed polynomial dependence on 1/ε may then be large. The interesting approximation regime fixes accuracy while n and the optimum rank vary.
